verdicts.rewritten_summary: BBC (28 Jul 2016): same-sex marriage took effect on the island after Royal Assent of the Marriage and Civil Partnership Act (2015-16 law reform); the first civil-partnership-to-marriage conversion was completed days after entry into force, with civil partnerships (legal since 2011) convertible without a second ceremony — confirming a smooth, routine registration process for couples.

BBC (30 Nov 2005): the House of Keys adopted an Employment Bill amendment protecting gay and lesbian employees from dismissal on sexual-orientation grounds (tabling by Onchan MHK Peter Karran) — the island's employment non-discrimination milestone, aligned with UK human-rights law.

3FM (9 Jun 2015): Chief Minister Allan Bell publicly backed same-sex marriage and said he would formulate a bill to repeal the island's marriage prohibition — the political commitment that preceded the 2016 Marriage and Civil Partnership Act.

HRW (26 Mar 2026): the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill amends the 2019 law to limit legal recognition to historically accepted socio-cultural groups (hijra, kinner) and intersex individuals — removing recognition for those self-identifying as trans men, trans women or non-binary; rights activists (e.g. Akkai Padmashali) call it criminalising and an attack on the right to exist. Parliament passed it in March 2026.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: BBC: India's parliament passed the controversial amendment redefining how transgender people are legally recognised, dropping self-identification amid opposition and LGBTQ-community protests; government frames it as widening welfare access and anti-trafficking protection, critics say it excludes many trans/non-binary/gender-fluid people. India has an estimated ~2 million transgender people.
